title: Monitoring, Governance & Secrets
oneLiner: See what's happening and keep it compliant: CloudWatch, CloudTrail, AWS Config, Secrets Manager, and SSM.
examWeightNote: Rounds out Design Secure Architectures — observability, auditing, compliance, and secret handling.
objectives: Tell apart CloudWatch (metrics/logs/alarms), CloudTrail (API audit), and AWS Config (resource compliance).
Use CloudWatch alarms and dashboards to react to metrics and drive Auto Scaling.
Store and rotate secrets with Secrets Manager; use SSM Parameter Store for config.
Apply Trusted Advisor checks for security, cost, and best practices.

services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
services.purpose: Metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards for AWS resources and applications.

services.name: AWS CloudTrail
services.purpose: Records every API call for auditing, security analysis, and troubleshooting.

services.name: AWS Config
services.purpose: Tracks resource configuration over time and evaluates it against compliance rules.

services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
services.purpose: Stores, encrypts, and automatically rotates secrets like DB credentials and API keys.

services.name: SSM Parameter Store
services.purpose: Hierarchical storage for configuration and secrets (free standard tier; integrates with KMS).

services.name: AWS Trusted Advisor
services.purpose: Automated checks and recommendations across cost, security, performance, and resilience.

keyConcepts: CloudWatch = 'how is it performing?' — metrics, logs, dashboards, and alarms (alarms can trigger Auto Scaling or notifications).
CloudTrail = 'who did what?' — an audit log of API calls across the account; essential for security forensics and compliance.
AWS Config = 'is it compliant and how did it change?' — records configuration history and evaluates resources against rules.
Secrets Manager stores and automatically rotates secrets (e.g. RDS credentials); prefer it over hard-coding or env files.
SSM Parameter Store holds configuration and secrets hierarchically; the standard tier is free and can encrypt values with KMS (SecureString).
Trusted Advisor surfaces best-practice recommendations; the full set of checks requires Business/Enterprise Support.

diagram.caption: Three complementary lenses on your account, plus managed secrets for apps.
diagram.note: Remember the one-liners: CloudWatch = performance, CloudTrail = who-did-what, Config = compliance/history.

scenarios.scenario: A security team needs to know exactly who deleted a security group and when, across the whole account.
scenarios.question: Which service provides this audit trail?
scenarios.explanation: CloudTrail records API calls (who, what, when, from where) — the go-to for auditing and security forensics. CloudWatch is about performance metrics/logs, not an API audit trail.

scenarios.scenario: An application hard-codes database credentials in its config, and the team wants them encrypted and rotated automatically.
scenarios.question: What should they use?

options.label: AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation
Store them in a public S3 bucket
Leave them in the code but add a comment

scenarios.explanation: Secrets Manager stores and encrypts secrets and can rotate them automatically (e.g. RDS credentials), removing hard-coded secrets from code/config.

quiz.question: Which service records API calls for auditing 'who did what' in your account?
quiz.explanation: CloudTrail is the account-wide API audit log — essential for security analysis and compliance.

quiz.question: Amazon CloudWatch is primarily for:
options: Metrics, logs, dashboards, and alarms (performance/operational monitoring)
quiz.answer: Metrics, logs, dashboards, and alarms (performance/operational monitoring)
quiz.explanation: CloudWatch answers 'how is it performing?' and its alarms can trigger scaling or notifications.

quiz.question: AWS Config is used to:
options: Track resource configuration history and evaluate compliance against rules
quiz.answer: Track resource configuration history and evaluate compliance against rules
quiz.explanation: Config records how resources are configured over time and flags non-compliant settings.

quiz.question: The best way to store and automatically rotate database credentials is:
options: A plaintext file on the instance
quiz.explanation: Secrets Manager encrypts secrets and supports automatic rotation, integrating with services like RDS.

quiz.question: Which statement about SSM Parameter Store is correct?
options: It is only for EC2 user data
It stores config/secrets hierarchically, with a free standard tier and KMS-encrypted SecureString values
quiz.answer: It stores config/secrets hierarchically, with a free standard tier and KMS-encrypted SecureString values
quiz.explanation: Parameter Store holds configuration and secrets; SecureString values are encrypted with KMS. It's a lighter-weight option than Secrets Manager (which adds managed rotation).

quiz.question: A CloudWatch alarm on high CPU can automatically:
options: Trigger an Auto Scaling action or send an SNS notification
quiz.answer: Trigger an Auto Scaling action or send an SNS notification
quiz.explanation: Alarms react to metric thresholds — e.g. scaling out an Auto Scaling group or notifying via SNS.
